author: Tim
title: Hallmark Star's Sudden Passing Stuns Fans
text:
Nathaniel Nate Pelletier passed away suddenly at home on April 11 and he was only 53 years old. His obituary said he died while alone in his home in Langley and it came as a shock to everyone who loved him.
He was born in Toronto back in 1971 and people knew him for being generous and for working hard at just about anything he did. Friends also talked about how his charisma made him easy to be around and how he always tried to help people when they needed it.
Nate worked behind the scenes on When Calls the Heart in the transportation department and he sometimes showed up on screen as the taxi driver. People on set called him N8 and he got close to a few of the guys there like Gord, Trevor, and Andrew who they called Pikachu.
His daughter, Myhrsades Murray Jones, was the center of his world and he loved taking her to concerts and on little trips whenever they could. It seems like she brought out the happiest side of him and he made sure she always felt supported.
When he was off work he liked to cook and bake and he wrote poetry when the mood hit him. His home was one of those places where people felt comfortable and he would stand out on the balcony giving hugs or be in the kitchen laughing with whoever stopped by.
Martin Cummins who plays Henry Gowen shared a long tribute online talking about how much Nate meant to him.
He said: “I just came back from a ride on the bike Gord and Nate put together for the girls and I. I’m taking shade in Mexico under the awning Nate helped me figure out in the woods near the old cabin. I have spent more hours at work sitting in the blue room, in silence or in conversation with Gord and Nate than I have standing on tape with the camera rolling. Gord has always felt like a father figure to me, and Nate and I were his boys running around the town, hanging out in the woods and talking shit. Life is constantly changing. Things are never the same. The Valley will not be the same without Nathaniel Pelletier. He was a gentle soul and it was my honor to call him friend.”
The tribute shows how much this loss hit the people who worked with him and how many memories they shared. It is clear he meant a lot more to them than what you see on screen.
